source.title: The two clocks and the innovation window: When and how generative models learn rules
source.authors: Binxu Wang; Emma Finn; Bingbin Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study trains generative models on synthetic rule-governed datasets and measures rule-valid generation and memorization over training, using metrics and objectives different from standard training/test accuracy.
record.gate_note: The study directly measures rule accuracy, memorization, and their timing, as well as DSM and nearest-neighbor progress measures. It does not report standard training accuracy. It also evaluates optimization sweeps, but does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifacts. Numerous additional task variants and plotted curves are not individually recorded below.
record.test_reason: The study tracks generative models (DiT, GPT) on rule-governed synthetic data, measuring when generations become rule-valid (τrule) and when they start reproducing training samples (τmem). Generalization comes first and memorization later, the reverse of grokking's order. No training-accuracy saturation precedes the rule jump. Grokking is cited only to say the GPT weight-decay result is 'consistent with the grokking literature'. This is a related but different construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find two clocks: τrule rises with rule complexity and falls with model capacity, while τmem scales near-linearly with N and is roughly rule-invariant. Their gap is an innovation window that widens with N and can close at high G. The structure holds for DiT and GPT, and the transitions correspond to attractor-basin changes. Missing from the paraphrase: rule learning precedes memorization, and GPT has shorter timescales.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains diffusion and autoregressive generative models on synthetic rule-valid distributions and tracks generated-sample validity and memorization, rather than reporting the conventional training/test-accuracy trajectory named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Rule-learning time changes with rule complexity, model capacity, and in some settings dataset size. Memorization onset changes with dataset size, model capacity, architecture, and GPT weight decay. Learning rate affects both transitions; input encoding also changes memorization timing in categorical tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: In DiT and GPT generative models on parity, rule-valid generation emerges sharply (chance to >0.9) before memorization. τrule rises about tenfold per unit of G. τmem scales near-linearly with N and is roughly independent of the rule.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In generative models on rule-governed data, rule learning precedes memorization. Memorization onset scales with dataset size, opening an 'innovation window' (the reverse of grokking's order).

fits_no_version.finding: Loss splits (DSM or cross-entropy) and nearest-neighbor distance anticipate the sample-level transitions. Attractor basins of training samples gradually grow after rule learning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continuous loss and landscape measures anticipate rule-learning and memorization transitions in generative models.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-mini, weight decay delays memorization, with λ=0.3 maximizing the rule-to-memorization gap. In DiT-mini, weight decay has no strong effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight decay suppresses memorization more than rule learning in autoregressive generative models, but not in diffusion models.

record.problems: The main timing and accuracy trajectories are often presented in figures without exact numerical values in the text. The paper reports run-to-run variability near the G≈6 learnability frontier. Its measures are generated rule validity and memorization, not conventional training/test accuracy, and the paper does not identify the specific circuit or algorithm proposed in V2.
record.rows_left_out: Under the 60-row limit, omitted per-G and per-N curves and fits beyond the aggregate scaling results; individual task/encoding results for exact-K, row-K, Latin square, and Sudoku; and detailed per-setting learning-rate and weight-decay sweep outcomes. These are primarily in Figs. 8–10, 20–27 and Sections C.2–C.7.

untested.parts: Training-accuracy saturation followed by a delayed test-accuracy jump is not measured; generalization precedes memorization here.
No generalizing circuit, Fourier algorithm, or removal of memorizing components is studied.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale or lazy-to-rich manipulation.
No norm or efficiency measurement, no critical dataset size, no ungrokking.
Learned algorithms are not compared across runs.
No test of optimizer instability or floating-point artifacts.

record.verdict_notes: The reader treated rule accuracy as test accuracy and memorization as the training fit, then scored V1 and V2. Grokking requires generalization after overfitting; here generalization comes first, and no training-accuracy saturation precedes the rule jump. So the study is recorded as discussing, not testing, the claim. One could argue it gives grokking-adjacent evidence for V5 through GPT weight decay, but it has no efficiency or critical-size test.

versions.untested_parts: It does not measure standard training accuracy saturating or conventional test accuracy. It measures generated rule validity and sample memorization instead.
It does not identify a Fourier algorithm or decompose the model into generalizing and memorizing circuits/components.
No non-algorithmic image, text, or molecule training setting, initialization-scale sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition is tested.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
The study does not measure whether weight decay selects a lower-norm or more efficient circuit, nor a critical dataset size or ungrokking below it.
Repeated runs are examined for timing variability, but the study does not identify or compare the algorithms learned across runs.
Learning-rate and weight-decay sweeps are reported, but adaptive-optimizer instabilities and floating-point or softmax limitations are not controlled or tested as proposed causes.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Train on group-parity data and track generated sample-level rule accuracy.
rows.measure: τrule: first step sample-level rule accuracy reliably exceeds 0.9
rows.locator: Section 3, Determinants of rule-learning time; Fig. 2C
rows.note: The reported rule-validity onset is a generated-sample measure, not conventional test accuracy.
rows.check: Measures onset of generated-sample rule validity, with no prior training-accuracy saturation. It does not measure V1's delayed generalization after overfitting.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Train on group-parity data and track generated sample-level rule accuracy.
rows.measure: τrule: first step sample-level rule accuracy reliably exceeds 0.9
rows.locator: Section 3, Determinants of rule-learning time; Fig. 2C
rows.note: The detailed mechanism analysis also describes a rule-learning checkpoint at step 119k; the main scaling summary gives approximately 10^4 steps.
rows.check: Same as R1. The ~10^4-step figure is from the scaling summary. Sec. 4 places the rule transition between the 14k and 119k checkpoints.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Train on group-parity data and track generated sample-level rule accuracy.
rows.measure: τrule: first step sample-level rule accuracy reliably exceeds 0.9
rows.locator: Section 3, Determinants of rule-learning time; Fig. 2C
rows.note: The authors describe roughly an order-of-magnitude delay per unit increase in G for these small G values.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Train on group-parity data and track rule learning and memorization onsets.
rows.measure: Reliability of rule-learning transition relative to memorization onset
rows.value: The transition becomes unreliable; the authors say τrule likely approaches τmem and the innovation window begins to close.
rows.locator: Section 3, Determinants of rule-learning time; Fig. 2C
rows.note: This is described as a near-frontier setting, not a consistently observed transition.
rows.check: Describes an unreliable transition near the learnability frontier. It is not a grokking measure.

rows.subject: DiT models at all tested sizes
rows.size_stated: DiT-nano, DiT-mini, and DiT-B; sizes stated as ∼2.2M, ∼16.5M, and ∼129.5M parameters
rows.operation_detail: Train on group-parity data and track rule accuracy through the training budget.
rows.value: Rules with G ≥ 9 are not acquired within 10^6 steps; final accuracy is attributed to later memorization.
rows.note: The text says the largest tested 12-layer model also fails at G ≥ 9.
rows.check: Failure to learn high-G parity. It is not a grokking measure.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Vary dataset size and compare rule-learning curves.
rows.measure: Effect of dataset size on τrule
rows.value: Curves are described as indistinguishable across N for G=2 and G=3; τrule mildly increases with N for G=4 and G=6.
rows.locator: Section 3, Determinants of rule-learning time; Fig. 2D(i), G
rows.note: The direction for G=4 and G=6 is toward a mild increase with larger, not smaller, datasets; the study does not report standard training accuracy.
rows.check: Marked 'reversed' against V1's dataset-size clause, but τrule here is not a delay after training saturation. Not comparable to V1.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Vary dataset size and measure the memorization onset.

conditions.value: multiple dataset sizes; fit across all G

rows.value: τmem ≈ 35 N^1.14 (R2 = 0.94, n = 34); the text describes the scaling as nearly linear.
rows.locator: Section 3, Determinants of memorization time; Fig. 2D(ii)
rows.note: This is the study-reported aggregate fit across G, rather than an average reconstructed across separate conditions.
rows.check: Memorization onset scaling with N. It concerns the timing of overfitting, not delayed generalization.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Vary dataset size at G=6 and compare rule-learning and memorization onset.
rows.measure: Whether rule learning occurs before memorization
rows.value: G=6 is not learned at N=1024 or 2048, but is learned at N=4k, 8k, and 16k as the τmem ceiling rises.
rows.note: Larger datasets permit rule acquisition in this setting, rather than smaller datasets requiring more optimization.
rows.check: Larger N lets the rule be learned before memorization. Under V1 this is not 'reversed', because the construct differs.

rows.subject: GPT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Train autoregressively on group-parity data and track rule validity and memorization.
rows.baseline: Rule accuracy chance level is 2^-D/G at the sample level; memorization baseline depends on the distribution.
rows.value: For simpler rules G ≤ 6, the text reports a rule-learning transition followed by a later memorization transition.
rows.uncertainty: Run-to-run variation is described near G=6; see Fig. 28.
rows.note: The two transitions are generative rule-validity and sample-memorization measures, not standard training/test accuracy.
rows.check: GPT shows rule learning followed by later memorization, which is the opposite ordering to grokking. It does not show V1's delayed generalization.

rows.subject: GPT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Vary dataset size and measure the memorization onset.
rows.note: The paper describes the scaling as near-linear.
rows.check: Memorization-time scaling for GPT. Not a V1 measure.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate DSM losses on training, held-out rule-valid, and random Boolean-cube samples during training.

conditions.value: σ ∈ [0.2, 2.0] for the reported train/held-out split

rows.measure: DSM-loss separation between training and held-out rule-valid samples
rows.baseline: Before the memorization onset, training and held-out losses are described as not separated.
rows.value: Around τmem, training and held-out losses diverge; the separation is reported over σ ∈ [0.2, 2.0]. The loss split occurs before the sample-defined τmem.
rows.note: This is a continuous loss-based signal preceding the sample-level memorization threshold; numeric loss values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Shows a DSM loss split anticipating memorization onset. It is not a progress measure for a delayed generalizing circuit as V2 names.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Track nearest-training-sample Hamming distance of generated samples through late training.
rows.measure: Nearest-neighbor Hamming distance to the training set
rows.value: The distance decays during late training, including for rule-valid non-memorized generations, before exact memorization onset.
rows.note: The authors characterize this as gradual contraction toward training samples before exact memorization.
rows.check: Gradual drift of generations toward training samples before memorization. It concerns memorization, not the formation of a generalizing circuit.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Track rule-valid and rule-violating attractor basins in a fixed two-dimensional slice of the learned vector field.
rows.measure: Relative basin sizes for rule-valid and rule-violating samples
rows.baseline: At step 14k, the four reference points have similar-sized, symmetric basins.
rows.value: At step 119k, rule-valid basins expand sharply and rule-violating basins shrink; training and held-out valid basins remain roughly symmetric.
rows.note: The text describes the landscape change; it does not identify a Fourier circuit.
rows.check: The text calls the rule-learning basin change sudden and synchronized ('sharp', 'suddenly'). No continuous measure anticipating it is shown, and there is no circuit.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Track training-sample attractor-basin expansion after rule learning.
rows.measure: Training-sample basin relative to a held-out valid neighbor
rows.baseline: At step 119k, the two valid reference basins are described as roughly symmetric.
rows.value: By step 492k, the training-sample basin expands into the held-out valid neighbor's basin; the onset is described as gradual.
rows.note: This supports later growth of training-sample attraction, not a reported removal of a memorizing circuit.
rows.check: Training-sample basin expansion, i.e. memorization growing. This is the opposite of V2's memorizing components being removed.

rows.subject: GPT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate next-token cross-entropy on training, held-out rule-valid, and random Boolean samples.
rows.measure: Cross-entropy loss separation across data splits
rows.baseline: Before the corresponding transitions, the losses are not described as separated.
rows.value: Boolean-cube loss separates from training and held-out rule-valid losses at rule learning; training and held-out losses separate at memorization.
rows.note: The study reports distinct loss divergences but does not decompose the network into circuits.
rows.check: Loss splits mark the GPT transitions. No mechanism is identified as V2 describes.

rows.subject: GPT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Sweep weight decay while tracking rule-learning and memorization onsets.
rows.measure: Memorization onset and gap between rule-learning and memorization onsets
rows.value: Increasing weight decay generally delays τmem; λ=3×10^-1 maximizes the temporal gap. At λ ≥ 1, both transitions slow and the separation is reduced.
rows.note: A larger gap is reported at moderate weight decay, but the proposed low-norm/efficient-circuit explanation is not tested.
rows.check: Weight decay delays memorization and widens the rule–memorization gap. There is no test of circuit efficiency, critical dataset size or ungrokking.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Sweep weight decay while tracking rule-learning and memorization onsets.
rows.value: The authors report no strong effect of weight decay on τrule or τmem in the explored range; τmem remains near late training for successful runs.
rows.note: The main text separately says very large weight decay, including wd=10^-2 in the figure description, delays and weakens rule acquisition.
rows.check: No strong DiT weight-decay effect was found. Not a V5 measure.

rows.subject: DiT-mini
rows.operation_detail: Sweep weight decay while tracking rule-learning onset.
rows.value: This setting does not reach the rule-learning criterion within the training budget, according to the figure description.
rows.note: The text also summarizes the overall weight-decay effect as not strong across the explored range.
rows.check: At wd=10^-2 the DiT fails to reach the rule criterion. Not a V5 measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: DiT-mini rule-onset sweep across N, including G=2–6
reader_labels.reason: Rule-learning time is indistinguishable across N for G=2 and G=3 and mildly increases with larger N for G=4 and G=6; the results do not show smaller datasets requiring more optimization for rule acquisition (R6, R8).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: DiT-mini at G=2–4, N=4096, and GPT-mini on simpler parity rules
reader_labels.reason: The study reports a rule-validity transition followed by later memorization, with τrule increasing from approximately 10^3 to 10^5 as G rises (R1-R3, R9). It does not measure training-accuracy saturation.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: DiT-mini and GPT-mini on parity tasks
reader_labels.reason: DSM and cross-entropy splits, declining nearest-neighbor distances, and changes in attractor basins provide progress measures or mechanistic changes around or before the sample-level transitions (R11-R15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Mechanistic interpretation of the measured transitions
reader_labels.reason: The study does not identify a Fourier algorithm or show that a memorizing circuit is removed; it instead reports score losses, distances, and attractor-landscape changes (R11-R15).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-mini, G=6, N=4096, moderate-to-large weight decay
reader_labels.reason: Increasing weight decay generally delays memorization, with λ=3×10^-1 maximizing the rule-to-memorization gap (R16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: DiT-mini weight-decay sweep and the proposed efficiency account
reader_labels.reason: The study reports no strong overall effect on DiT memorization timing, and does not measure norms, circuit efficiency, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking (R17-R18).
